stories.title: The hospital that paid
stories.text: A hospital app had an exported content provider. Attackers read patient records through it, then encrypted the database. The hospital paid the ransom.

stories.title: The update that was not
stories.text: Attackers bought an abandoned popular app and pushed an update that was ransomware. 100000 users updated without thinking.

stories.title: The flashlight that saw everything
stories.text: A free flashlight app requested 23 permissions including camera, contacts, SMS. 50 million users installed it. It exfiltrated data for 3 years.

stories.title: The clipboard thief
stories.text: A popular social media app was caught reading clipboard contents every time opened. Users who copied passwords or crypto seeds had them silently sent away.

stories.title: The backup that leaked millions
stories.text: A banking app enabled adb backup. Researchers extracted the entire database including credit card numbers and encryption keys.

stories.title: The HTTP banking app
stories.text: A regional bank mobile app used HTTP for login. An attacker on WiFi captured 200 customer credentials in one afternoon.

stories.title: The hardcoded AWS keys
stories.text: Developers hardcoded AWS access keys in a fitness app. Attackers found them via decompilation and racked up 50000 dollars in mining charges.

stories.title: The debug build in production
stories.text: A startup released a debug build to 1 million users. Attackers used adb to attach debuggers and extract user data.

stories.title: The fake login screen
stories.text: Malware used tapjacking overlays to draw fake login screens over banking apps. Users typed credentials into the attacker UI.

stories.title: The hijacked deep link
stories.text: A food delivery app used custom URL schemes for OAuth. A malicious app registered the same scheme and stole 500000 tokens.

stories.title: The implicit intent leak
stories.text: A messaging app sent photos via implicit intents. Any matching app could receive them. A spy app collected intimate photos.

stories.title: The mutable pending intent
stories.text: A notification service created mutable pending intents. Attackers modified them to send SMS from victims phones.

stories.title: The world-readable database
stories.text: A note-taking app stored notes with MODE_WORLD_READABLE. Any app could read private notes including saved passwords.

stories.title: The log that leaked tokens
stories.text: A developer forgot to remove Log statements printing OAuth tokens. A competing app read logs and stole sessions.

stories.title: The WebView XSS
stories.text: A news app loaded articles in WebView with JavaScript enabled. Malicious articles injected JavaScript that stole cookies.

stories.title: The certificate not pinned
stories.text: A financial app used HTTPS but no pinning. Attackers with physical access installed a CA cert and intercepted all traffic.

stories.title: The SharedPreferences password
stories.text: A fitness app stored passwords in plain text SharedPreferences. When phone was sent for repair, credentials were extracted.

stories.title: The exported activity
stories.text: A car companion app had exported activity that could remotely start engine. Attackers started 100 cars as proof of concept.

stories.title: The SQL injection
stories.text: A contact manager had content provider vulnerable to SQL injection. Attackers extracted entire database via crafted URIs.

stories.title: The broadcast spy
stories.text: A utility registered for BOOT_COMPLETED and SMS_RECEIVED without permissions. It sent all SMS to a command server.
